expectation: Membrane ring on a subset of CD45+ leukocytes (naive T cells, B cells, NK cells). It should be dense in lymphoid aggregates or follicles (B cells) and appear as scattered single lymphocytes in stroma; tumour epithelium should be negative.
observed: A: dense, sharply bounded yellow aggregates in several tiles (lymphoid-follicle-like) plus scattered single cells; most other tiles are dark. B/C: sparse discrete small cells in stroma. D: packed cells with ring-like membrane signal around dark nuclei.
why: Dense aggregates that look like lymphoid follicles and scattered single cells with membrane rings, all on a dark background, show a specific lymphocyte population.
notes: CD45RA lights compact lymphoid-like aggregates and scattered single cells. At close range it is a membrane ring around nuclei, and most of the tissue is negative, which is what a real naive-lymphocyte/B-cell stain looks like.
